summary: Antigua and Barbuda waives visas for citizens of the 102 countries and territories on the Immigration Department's visa-exemption list (as of 8 October 2026), including the US, Canada, the UK, the EU and most Commonwealth countries, normally for stays of up to six months — while everyone else applies for an eVisa online (or at a mission) before traveling, unless they hold a US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa, which qualifies them for a USD 100 visa on arrival.

conditionalWaivers.text: Travellers who need a visa but hold a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa or residence card can get a single-entry Tourist Visa-on-Arrival for up to 30 days, for USD 100 per passenger (children included). It is for tourism or visiting friends and relatives only, cannot be extended or converted except on medical grounds, and requires a passport valid for six months, a return ticket and enough money for the stay.

fee.notes: Per passenger, children included, payable on arrival (or the equivalent in Eastern Caribbean dollars). Only for travellers who hold a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa or residence card; not available to diplomatic or official passport holders.

fee.notes: Non-CARICOM nationals; CARICOM nationals pay XCD 150. A processing fee only — it does not guarantee the extension. Apply in person at the Immigration Department in St John's before your entry stamp expires; each extension is for up to three months.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers aged one year and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, including after more than 12 hours' transit through an airport in one. WHO's risk list includes Trinidad and Tobago.

source.name: WHO, International Travel and Health, Annex 1 — countries requiring proof of vaccination against yellow fever
source.instrument: International Health Regulations (2005), Article 36 and Annex 7; WHO International Travel and Health, Annex 1, 18 November 2022 (revised 3 January 2023)

travelInsurance.text: No official source makes insurance a condition of entry for ordinary visits. The UK government advises adequate travel health insurance: treatment can be expensive and serious cases may need an emergency evacuation.

onwardTicket.text: The Immigration Department says visa-exempt visitors must have an onward or return ticket and confirmation of accommodation.

source.name: Antigua and Barbuda Immigration Department — General Visa Information

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors must be able to show evidence that they can maintain themselves during their stay, alongside an onward or return ticket and confirmed accommodation. No fixed amount is published.

declarations.name: ArriveAntigua online arrival form
declarations.text: The UK Foreign Office says the Antiguan and Barbudan authorities advise travellers to use ArriveAntigua to speed up entry, though it is not mandatory, and that it can only be accessed on a mobile phone or tablet within 72 hours of travel.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Antigua and Barbuda travel advice (entry requirements)

currencyLimits.text: On arrival you must declare cash, cheques or money orders worth more than USD 10,000 or the equivalent in other currencies, according to Canada's travel advice. No Antiguan government page we could read states the threshold.

source.name: Government of Canada — Antigua and Barbuda travel advice (money)

notes: The UK Foreign Office says there are strict rules on goods you can take into or out of Antigua and Barbuda, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.
Canada's travel advice says it is an offence to wear camouflage clothing or to carry or import items made from camouflage material; items are confiscated and offenders can be fined or jailed.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says there have been incidents of violent crime, including murder, armed robbery and sexual assault, and advises avoiding isolated areas, including beaches, particularly after dark. Canada says petty crime such as pickpocketing and purse snatching increases with the approach of annual festivities. The UK says currents can be deceptively strong and not all beaches have lifeguards.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says an International Driving Permit is not recognized; you need a temporary local driver's licence, bought on presentation of your home licence. The UK Foreign Office says car hire companies usually help, or you can get one from the Transport Board or a police station. Traffic drives on the left.
Canada's travel advice says the hurricane season runs from early June to the end of November, and that even small tropical storms can quickly become major hurricanes.
Canada's travel advice says US dollars are widely accepted. The UK Foreign Office says taxis are not metered and fares are set by zone: agree the fare in local currency before you set off.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Antigua and Barbuda?
faq.answer: Antigua and Barbuda waives visas for citizens of the 102 countries and territories on the Immigration Department's visa-exemption list (as of 8 October 2026), including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, the EU and most Commonwealth countries — visitors are normally admitted for up to six months. Everyone else needs a visitor visa before traveling, applied for online through the Immigration Department’s eVisa system or at an Antigua and Barbuda mission. Travellers who hold a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa or residence card can instead buy a 30-day Tourist Visa-on-Arrival for USD 100.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Antigua and Barbuda without a visa?
faq.answer: The Immigration Department says visitors may be granted permission to land for up to six months, and visa-exempt visitors may stay as long as their business takes within that limit. An extension, for up to three months at a time, is applied for in person at the Immigration Department, for a fee, before the entry endorsement expires.

faq.question: How much passport validity do I need?
faq.answer: The Immigration Department says your passport must be valid beyond the date of your return ticket. For the Tourist Visa-on-Arrival it asks for six months' validity.

faq.question: Do I need a return ticket?
faq.answer: Yes. The Immigration Department says visitors must have an onward or return ticket and confirmation of accommodation, and may be asked to show they can support themselves during the stay.

faq.question: Can I work remotely from Antigua and Barbuda?
faq.answer: Not through the Nomad Digital Residence: its official website (nomad.gov.ag) now states that the programme has ended.
